marks.gloss_en: Abaye: rather, here [the baraita speaks of] a tree standing in the private domain whose boughs lean into the public domain, and one threw and it came to rest on its boughs
מאי טעמא? -- at nine handbreadths the many certainly adjust their burdens on it
a pillar nine handbreadths high in the public domain, on which the many adjust their burdens: one threw and it rested on top -- he is liable
מאי טעמא? -- תשמיש על ידי הדחק לא שמיה תשמיש
Rav Yosef: and so in a hole [Ulla's rule applies]
איתיביה... וכן בגומא. מאי לאו אסיפא? -- the baraita's 'and so with a hole' refers to the latter clause: one may carry from a hole under ten, so a hole is like the public domain
לא, ארישא -- 'and so with a hole' refers to the first clause (ten deep and four wide: no carrying)

the baraita: if his basket lay in the public domain, ten high and four wide, one may not carry from it to the public domain or from the public domain into it; less than that, one may; and so with a hole
איתיביה: the eiruv baraita, read of a pit not ten deep (8b.3), rules his eiruv valid -- אלמא תשמיש על ידי הדחק שמיה תשמיש
one threw a reed barrel into the public domain, ten [handbreadths] high and not six wide: he is liable (Abaye asserts; Rava denies -- even so, exempt)
what is the reason? it is impossible that the reed-ends not rise above ten
if he overturned it on its mouth: seven and a bit [high] -- liable
what is the reason? partitions are made for their inside
